doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Grimes's UN project 'Deep Tones for Peace'
summary: Grimes describes a New York-Jerusalem all-bassist event; Ali asks about Omer Avital.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I wanted to ask about a few current things before we sort of go back in time a little bit. Henry, did you just do something at the UN I read about?

Yes we just did something that’s going to be going on between New York and Jerusalem, where, a couple of months from now, and it’s going to be all bassists in Israel and New York, I mean not Israel, Jerusalem and New York.
How many bass players is that?
It’s some Israeli bass players too?
Omer Avital, was he on that?
Omer Avital, he’s a great bass player from Israel.
Is it called “Deep Tones for Peace?”
Yeah “Deep Tones for Peace.” You heard of it?
I read it in your information. It sounds fascinating.
